newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Standard Chartered completes Nigeria sale.
newsitem.headline: Standard Chartered completes Nigeria sale.

text.p: Standard Chartered Bank Plc's divestment from Nigeria's First Bank has now been completed, sources at the issuing house said on Friday.

The executives of Stanbic Merchant Bank, which was in charge of the sale of 66.5 million shares representing Standard Chartered's 9.9 percent stake in First Bank, said the issue was heavily oversubscribed.
"The offer was 339.40 percent subscribed," said one.
Investors demanded 225.9 million shares, well over the volume on offer, the sources said.
"It is not surprising that many investors wanted to buy the shares," said Tunde Ayeni, a trader with CSL Stockbrokers.
"At 6.00 naira per share, the price was right," he added.
The current price of First Bank shares on the Nigerian Stock Exchange is 7.10 naira.
Analysts said First Bank's record of paying well above average dividend must have also endeared it to the public.
Standard Bank said in June it was divesting from Nigeria's oldest bank to focus on its core international banking activities.
It said both would continue to relate on a correspondent basis. ($1=80 naira)
